'''Archibald Read Richardson''' [[Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name="frs"/> (21 August 1881 &ndash; 4 November 1954) was a British [[mathematician]] known for his work in [[algebra]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Turnbull | first1 = H. W. |  volume=s1-31 | doi = 10.1112/jlms/s1-31.3.376 | title = Archibald Read Richardson | journal = Journal of the London Mathematical Society | issue = 3 | pages = 376–384 | year = 1956 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Turnbull | first1 = H. W. | doi = 10.1017/S0950184300000343 | title = Archibald R. Richardson | journal = Edinburgh Mathematical Notes | volume = 40 | pages = 31–32 | year = 2008 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Richardson_Archibald}}</ref>

==Career==
Richardson collaborated with [[Dudley E. Littlewood]] on invariants and group representation theory.  They introduced [[the immanant of a matrix]], studied [[Schur polynomial|Schur functions]] and developed the [[Littlewood–Richardson rule]] for their multiplication.

==Awards and honours==
Richardson was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref name="frs"/> on 21 March 1946.
